class_balance.note: Rare-event classification -- scale_pos_weight used during training to correct for imbalance. Precision/Recall/F1/Balanced Accuracy/PR-AUC are the metrics that matter here, not plain accuracy.

split_note: Split by tender_id, not by row, since a single tender has multiple broker bids. Stratified so the rare positive class isn't concentrated on one side. NOT a chronological split -- this isn't a forecast-the-future problem the way the freight rate model is.
data_source: Synthetic data (bid_tender_records_synthetic.csv), provided by teammate. No real confirmed-collusion dataset exists for freight/maritime chartering specifically -- this is a proof-of-concept demonstrating the detection technique, not a claim of real detected corruption.

naive_baseline_comparison.description: Naive baseline = flag every bid that breaches the fair-value band, no ML at all.
naive_baseline_comparison.note: Model catches 87% of anomalies (vs naive's 100%) while flagging ~91% fewer bids for human review (209 vs 927).

references: Garcia Rodriguez et al. (2022), 'Collusion detection in public procurement auctions with machine learning algorithms', Automation in Construction
CCI (India) Diagnostic Toolkit for Public Procurement
